text.p: Citicorp executives told analysts Tuesday a key part of the company's strategy is reducing costs.

William Campbell, executive vice president and head of consumer banking, and Thomas Jones, executive vice president and principal financial officer, reviewed second-quarter earnings which were reported earlier in the day.

The earnings showed net income up eight percent from a year ago. In one key business, the global consumer business, net income fell three percent and in another, global corporate banking, net income was up five percent.

Revenue in the quarter also rose eight percent from a year ago. A questioner asked Jones to comment on the eight percent revenue growth in light of a 10-12 percent growth target. Jones said that if adjusted for currency movements, the revenue would be up 10 percent. He said in the current difficult competitive environment "10 percent revenue growth is nothing to be ashamed of."
Jones said the company has done "a decent job on costs" but "there is a chance to improve on that."
Campbell said the company is taking a "totally new approach to a global platform" which involves some standardization of systems and that will provide opportunities to reduce costs.
In a statement with the earnings, chairman and chief executive John Reed said the company will respond with "cost initiatives to accelerate the integration of our operations and technology base."
Asked by a reporter if the talk of cost reductions could involve layoffs, spokesman John Morris said it might but he added there are no plans now.
